# Running ZOOMAL-Flow one step at a time

*Generated by `scripts/py/render_walkthrough.py` — do NOT hand-edit. Regenerate with `snakemake walkthrough`.*

- Config the TUNABLES were resolved from: `config/cohort.example.yaml`
- Commit: `00e58db-dirty`

One page per stage, in run order. Each page says what the stage does, what it needs from the stage before it, the exact command to run up to it, and — per rule — what that rule does, which config keys steer it, what it writes, and how to re-run just that rule.

For the same material as one continuous read, see [`../WALKTHROUGH.md`](../WALKTHROUGH.md). Both are generated from the same rule docstrings in the same pass, so they cannot disagree.

## Stepping through manually

The pipeline does not have to be run in one go. Snakemake will stop where you tell it to, and pick up from there once you have looked at the output — which is the point of these pages: run a stage, check the figure or the table it produced, change a threshold or drop a bad sample, re-run that stage, carry on.

Four things do almost all of it:

| Invocation | What it does |
|---|---|
| `snakemake <output files>` | Build exactly those files and whatever they need, then stop. This is "run up to step N", and it is what each page prints. |
| `snakemake --force <output file>` | Re-run the one job that makes that file, and only it. This is "redo this step". |
| `snakemake --forcerun <rule>` | Re-run that rule *and everything downstream of it*. This is "I changed a setting, so redo this and everything computed from it". |
| `-n` (`--dry-run`) | Print what would run without running it. Worth doing before any `--forcerun`. |

Three things worth knowing before you rely on this:

- **Editing the config does not by itself trigger a re-run.** Snakemake decides what is out of date mostly from file timestamps, so after changing a threshold you have to force the rules it affects. That is what the force commands on each page are for.
- **`--forcerun` re-runs what comes after, too.** That is usually what you want — a changed threshold invalidates every figure drawn from it — but on a large cohort it is worth a `-n` first to see the size of what you just asked for. When you truly want one job and nothing else, use `--force <file>`.
- **`--until` is the obvious flag here, and it does not work past Stage 3.** Stage 3 ends in the `assign_clusters` checkpoint, which decides how many clusters exist and therefore which downstream jobs exist at all. `--until` prunes the graph before that is known and deadlocks with "Out of jobs ready to be started, but not all files built yet" ([snakemake#823](https://github.com/snakemake/snakemake/issues/823)). Naming the output files avoids the problem entirely, which is why these pages do that.

To edit an intermediate file by hand and keep it, `touch` it afterwards so it is newer than its inputs — otherwise the next run regenerates it and your edit is gone.

## The stages

| # | Stage | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Stage 0 — Setup](00_setup.md) | Preflight: sample roster, contig map, metadata validated against the role map. |
| 2 | [Stage 1 — QC](01_qc.md) | Filter to biallelic PASS SNPs on nuclear contigs, controls and masked regions removed. |
| 3 | [Stage 2 — MOI / Fws](02_moi.md) | Fws per sample — how mixed each infection is — and the high-MOI exclusion list. |
| 4 | [Stage 3 — Population structure](03_structure.md) | ADMIXTURE, PCA and NJ tree; picks K and assigns every sample to a cluster. |
| 5 | [Stage 4 — IBD and clonality](04_ibd.md) | Pairwise IBD within each cluster, clonal groups, and the two sample-set keep-lists. |
| 6 | [Stage 5 — Introgression](05_introgression.md) | Windows that look introgressed between each pair of clusters. |
| 7 | [Stage 6 — Selection (iHS)](06_selection.md) | rehh iHS scan, per case/control model declared in the config. |
| 8 | [Stage 7 — Comparison tables and the report](07_report.md) | Full vs de-clonalized comparison tables, then the self-contained HTML report. |
